what: Millicom sells mobile and home internet under the Tigo brand across Central and South America, in countries such as Guatemala, Colombia, Panama, Bolivia and Paraguay.
customers: Households and businesses in nine Latin American markets, mostly on prepaid mobile and fixed broadband.
moat: Networks built across markets where few operators compete, and in several of them Tigo is the leader with a brand that has been there for decades.
risks: Earnings are exposed to Latin American currencies, which can devalue sharply
Political and regulatory risk varies by country and is not always predictable
opportunities: 9.7 times free cash flow with $1.3B of free cash flow and a 22.6% margin
Analysts see about 25% upside, and the company has been buying back shares
Home broadband penetration in its markets is still far below developed country levels
watch: Service revenue growth in local currency, and free cash flow after capital spending.
